title: Final Parking Space: 1988 Chevrolet Nova Four-Door Sedan

body_markdown:
Toyota has been building vehicles at[its plant in Georgetown, Kentucky](https://pressroom.toyota.com/facility/toyota-motor-manufacturing-kentucky/) since the first Camry rolled off the line[in 1988](https://pressroom.toyota.com/toyota-car-kentucky-plant/) . More than three years before that, Americanized Toyota Sprinters began to be produced by the southeastern shore of the San Francisco Bay, at the joint GM-Toyota operation known as **N** ew **U** nited **M** otor **M** anufacturing, **I** nc. Here’s a discarded example of the original[NUMMI](https://www.toyota-global.com/company/history_of_toyota/75years/text/leaping_forward_as_a_global_corporation/chapter1/section3/item2_a.html) product, the Chevy Nova, spotted at[a car graveyard near Sacramento](https://www.picknpull.com/locations/52/rancho-cordova-ca) .


National Archives and Records Administration


This factory, located just off the Nimitz Freeway (then State Route 17, now Interstate 880), was GM’s Fremont Assembly. Its first vehicle, a C/K-series pickup, was born in 1963. As you can see from the cars in this photo of the plant taken on a smoggy day nine years later, General Motors products ruled American roads at the time.


General Motors


Fremont Assembly built[A-Body](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/definitive-1968-72-chevelle-ss-buyers-guide/) cars and[C/K-series](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/pickup-and-go-a-brief-history-of-the-c-k/) trucks through the rest of the 1960s and into the early 1980s, switching to the new front-wheel-drive A-Body[Chevrolet Celebrity](https://www.autoblog.com/news/junkyard-gem-1986-chevrolet-celebrity-eurosport-coupe/) and[Oldsmobile Cutlass Ciera](http://www.thetruthaboutcars.com/2018/04/junkyard-find-1982-oldsmobile-cutlass-ciera/) for its final year of 1982. Hostile relations between management and labor at the plant had resulted in increasing quality problems as the years went by; The General finally pulled the plug on Fremont Assembly in 1982. The above photograph shows the very last car built by Fremont Assembly: a[Cutlass Ciera in March of that year](https://www.upi.com/Archives/1982/03/03/Everyones-Out-at-GM-Fremont/7737383979600/) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The relationship between Toyota and GM goes *way* back. It began unofficially in 1935, when the Toyoda Automatic Loom Works took heavy inspiration from GM (engines) and Ford (truck chassis) when designing the[Toyoda Model G1](https://www.toyota-global.com/company/history_of_toyota/75years/vehicle_lineage/car/id60014785/) truck (soon after, the company name was changed to Toyo *t* a, because that pronunciation allows Japanese writers to use[a lucky number of strokes](https://support.toyota.com/s/article/What-is-the-origin-of-7650?language=en_US) to make the characters).


Aisin


Beginning in 1959, Toyota licensed the design of GM’s very successful Powerglide two-speed automatic transmission, resulting in the Toyoglide.


Toyota


[Aisin built](https://www.aisin.com/en/aithink/innovation/blog/005693.html) many of these transmissions for U.S.-market Coronas, Crowns, and Hiluxes. To this day, you’ll find common 1950s GM wheel bolt patterns on Toyota vehicles (though they are described in metric terms now).


Toyota


Though Toyota had become a major U.S.-market sales rival to GM by the early 1980s, GM executives realized that they needed to learn some essential production and management lessons from the now-mighty company from Nagoya. At the same time, Toyota sales in the United States were being squeezed by the Chicken Tax and threats of quotas on Japanese imports; the company needed a crash course on building cars in the United States in order to set up factories here. A deal was struck to create the[NUMMI joint venture](https://www.thisamericanlife.org/561/nummi-2015) on the site of Fremont Assembly, with American lineworkers being taught the tenets of[the Toyota Production System](https://global.toyota/en/company/vision-and-philosophy/production-system/) . The[E80-series Toyota Sprinter](https://www.toyota-global.com/company/history_of_toyota/75years/vehicle_lineage/car/id60009026A/index.html) , a member of the Corolla family, was chosen as the first model to be built.


Toyota


The E80 was the first Corolla to get front-wheel drive, although the platform also had rear-wheel-drive versions (including[the legendary AE86](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/this-1986-toyota-corolla-gt-s-ae86-turns-every-drive-into-a-tofu-run/) ). Toyota-badged[AE80 Corollas](https://www.toyota-global.com/company/history_of_toyota/75years/vehicle_lineage/car/id60003705A/index.html) first went on sale in the United States as 1984 models.


It’s more than new. It’s front-wheel drive!


Chevrolet Division, General Motors


Even as those new Corollas flew out of American Toyota showrooms, NUMMI was gearing up to build their Sprinter cousin in California. That car was the Nova, which was sold for the 1985-1988 model years.


Flickr/Alden Jewell


The Nova name was[well-known](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/68-74-nova-an-enthusiasts-blank-canvas/) to American car shoppers in 1985, thanks to three generations of Novas built during the span of the 1962-1979 model years.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


As the 1980s approached, the 1960s design of the original Nova had[become too archaic](https://www.autoblog.com/news/junkyard-gem-1979-chevrolet-nova-coupe/) to compete with more modern compact cars. Its replacement was[the Chevrolet Citation](https://autoweek.com/article/junkyard-treasures/junkyard-treasure-1980-chevrolet-citation-5-door-hatchback) , which debuted as a 1980 model.


Chevrolet Division, General Motors


Still, the Nova name (which began life as a trim-level designation for the Chevy II) was a recent and mostly fond memory for a couple of generations of American car shoppers by the mid-1980s. They remembered it as a simple, dependable car with a reasonable price tag. No, Spanish-speakers weren’t put off by the similarity to “no va” (“doesn’t go”); the car sold well in Mexico and other Latin American countries.


The initial TV commercials for the NUMMI Nova emphasized the car’s Japanese connections.


It’s telling that this commercial compares the 1987 Nova to a disreputable-looking 1977 Nova with lifted rear suspension and mag wheels, exactly the kind of car that mid-1980s solid citizens expected to be spinning donuts in the Circle K parking lot as[Dark Angel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8KfaTxBe4eM) blasted from its no-doubt-stolen cassette deck.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The NUMMI Nova was a success, with probably more than half a million units sold during four model years (I say “probably” because none of my reference books have sales figures for the 1985 car).


NUMMI added the Toyota-badged FX16 Corolla to its production lines for the 1987 model year, then switched to the new[E90 Corolla](https://www.toyota-global.com/company/history_of_toyota/75years/vehicle_lineage/car/id60003780/index.html) platform for the following year’s cars. Toyota pickups followed in 1992.


Once GM created[the Geo brand](https://www.murileemartin.com/Junkyard/JunkyardGallery-Geo.html) to sell cars designed and/or made by Toyota, Suzuki, and Isuzu, the Nova was replaced on the NUMMI line by the[E90 Sprinter](https://www.toyota-global.com/company/history_of_toyota/75years/vehicle_lineage/car/id60009134/index.html) -based Geo Prizm.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


We’ll get back to the history of the Fremont Assembly site in a bit, but now we’ll take a closer look at today’s FPS subject.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Interestingly, it was built as a “49-state” and Canadian-market car, not for sale in the state of California. I found it in a junkyard about equidistant from the Bay Area and the Reno-Carson City region, so it may have spent its early career in Nevada.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The final odometer reading was 165,978 miles, respectable for an economy car of its era but not[noteworthy for a Toyota](https://www.murileemartin.com/Junkyard/JunkyardGallery-300kMileCars.html) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The engine is a 1.6-liter SOCH 4A-LC engine, rated at 74 horsepower and 86 pound-feet. For 1988, it was possible to buy a[Nova Twin Cam 16-Valve Sedan](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Chevrolet/1988-Chevrolet/1988%20Chevrolet%20Nova/slides/1988%20Chevrolet%20Nova-14-15.html) (that’s the official model name) with a 110-horse version of the 4A-GE made famous in the AE86.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


A five-speed manual transmission was standard equipment; an automatic had to be purchased as part of an option package priced at either $645 or $1515 and including many other upgrades (those prices would be $1867 and $4386 in 2026 dollars).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The interior looks very nice for an affordable car pushing 40 years old.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I think those stains on the back seat happened after the car entered the junkyard ecosystem.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The September 1988 production date makes this one of the very last Chevy Novas ever built.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


NUMMI built cars and trucks for more than 25 years, nine more than Fremont Assembly. The final NUMMI product was[a red 2010 Corolla](https://global.toyota/en/detail/337166) . Later in 2010, Tesla bought the facility, and it has been[the Tesla Fremont Factory](https://www.tesla.com/fremont-factory) ever since.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Since I[found a 2013 Tesla Model S in a Colorado junkyard](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/a64355869/2013-tesla-model-s-is-junkyard-treasure/) last year, I can say that[I’ve documented used-up products](https://www.murileemartin.com/JunkyardGalleryHome.html) made by all three of the owners of the storied Fremont car factory.
